brief: RAIN CARVER: hydraulic erosion of a procedurally generated terrain, live in 3D. Generate a heightmap (fBm plus ridged noise, 256x256 desktop / 128x128 phone), then simulate particle-based droplet erosion (each droplet flows downhill with inertia, picks up sediment up to a capacity that depends on speed, slope and water, deposits the excess, evaporates; erosion applied with a small brush radius), tens of thousands of droplets per second in small batches per frame. Render in raw WebGL as a lit 3D mesh (normals recomputed as it erodes) with slope- and height-based colouring (rock, scree, grass, snow), an optional flow overlay showing where droplets travel so river networks emerge, and an orbit/zoom camera. Controls: new seed, erosion strength, rain rate, inertia, evaporation, deposition, a model-time counter clearly labelled as scaled, and a before/after split toggle. Pre-erode enough that the first frame already shows carved valleys.
